My birthday stay at this hotel was an absolute delight, and the service truly stood out. The front desk and housekeeping teams were incredibly thoughtful and attentive. Upon learning it was my birthday, they surprised me with fresh flowers and a birthday cake, and even upgraded me to a river view room free of charge. The room offered a spectacular, expansive view of the Huangpu River through its large panoramic windows, with the Oriental Pearl Tower and the Bund's architectural ensemble clearly visible. Both day and night views were absolutely stunning. The 87th-floor executive lounge was definitely a highlight, offering breathtaking 'cloud-level' views and creating an incredible ambiance for relaxation. The hotel is conveniently located in the Jin Mao Tower, right in the heart of Lujiazui, making transportation a breeze. Its classic atrium with a central void is very distinctive. While the facilities might show their age a bit, they are impeccably maintained. Whether it's for an anniversary or a 'Magic City' (Shanghai) getaway, if you want to experience Shanghai's high-altitude scenery, I highly recommend this place.

The Grand Hyatt Shanghai, a landmark hotel in Shanghai, lived up to expectations. Stepping into the 54th-floor lobby, one is immediately struck by its unique atmosphere, and the front desk staff are warm and attentive. The guest rooms are well-laid out, impeccably clean, and free of any musty odors.

The rooms were clean and comfortable, with meticulous attention to hygiene, making me feel very safe. The location is easy to find, with numerous attractions nearby, making sightseeing very convenient. The views are excellent, especially the night view. The service was patient and attentive; highly recommended.

The room was clean and tidy, and the bedding was so comfortable I didn't want to get out of bed. The bathroom was also very spacious. The views are stunning, especially the night view which is gorgeous, all lit up and really creating a great atmosphere!

The rooms are spacious and bright, providing stunning views of the Bund and the Huangpu River's night scenery right from your window. Throughout my stay, what impressed me most was the hotel's service. From the moment I entered, the concierge guided me and helped with my luggage, to the staff providing items upon request in the room, every single employee was polite, thoughtful, and quick to respond. The meticulous service, combined with high-end facilities, truly made me feel the kind of hospitality a five-star hotel should offer.

This was a spontaneous trip, and we booked this hotel specifically because of its proximity to Jin Mao Tower and Grand Hyatt. Our two-night stay left us with wonderful memories. Our twin room was on a high floor with an excellent view and plenty of space. The elevators were fast and responsive. The breakfast buffet offered a rich variety of dishes, with both Chinese and Western options being high quality. The fitness facilities were also quite unique, and our child even experienced their first sauna! I took a long-awaited vacation and stayed for four days, visiting the Oriental Pearl Tower, the Bund, and Xintiandi.

The hotel was excellent, needless to say. I enjoyed running, showering, and swimming. Although the prices were a bit high, the Japanese restaurant provided a welcome escape from the boredom of Chinese food, and I was satisfied with the night view and atmospheric dining at Cloud9.

I plan to visit frequently the next time I stay in Shanghai.

It was a vacation that reminded me of the importance of accommodation for a trip, and the sunrise in the last photo was fantastic.

Some people climb mountains to watch the sunrise, but wouldn't the sunrise be famous from a high-floor accommodation?

Excellent location, great view from the window, and big room. We chose a double bed room, which was very comfortable for our family of three. Due to the large number of customers during the Spring Festival, we had to wait in line for more than 20 minutes to check in.

I brought my parents to stay in Shanghai and they were very satisfied. Five-star hotel with five-star service, the service is very polite, thoughtful and warm. The lighting and bathing facilities in the room are easy to use and comfortable. Due to poor cervical spine, I have high requirements for pillows. Very satisfied, I'll definitely stay here again.

I was particularly pleased that when I requested a room change for a better view after checking in, the hotel managed to accommodate me despite the tight availability during the Mid-Autumn Festival. I'm very satisfied with that! 👍

The lobby is on the 54th floor, and taking the high-speed elevator directly from the ground to the clouds for check-in already feels very ritualistic, like "soaring into the sky." The heated swimming pool on the 57th floor faces the city skyline, offering a unique experience of swimming while gazing at the clouds. The fitness center is well-equipped with equally expansive views. The Executive Lounge's Happy Hour and food quality are also highly praised. The front desk and concierge staff are warm and professional, and enjoying the Bund night view from a west-facing room is delightful and comfortable!

The hotel boasts a dignified and elegant ambiance, making it ideal for business settings. Front desk procedures are efficient, and all inquiries are answered clearly and thoroughly. Guest rooms are quiet and comfortable, with ample desk space for easy work. Rooms are impeccably clean, and all facilities are in perfect working order.

Judy from the guest experience department was very considerate and the stay was great. The room has a great view, right on the Bund, and it's very convenient to go anywhere in the city center!
   For a little extra money, we upgraded the room type and provided breakfast for two adults and a child. There were many choices and the food was good.

The satisfaction of looking at the Shanghai skyline and knowing we stayed high up in the Jinmao tower is priceless.  It must be said however the room felt dated, our bathroom door broke and some unknown humming sound persisted throughout the night.

My first stay at Grand Hyatt Jin Mao exceeded all expectations! The hotel lobby on the 54th floor offers stunning views the moment you walk in.

I stayed in a 71st-floor river view room, and at night, the Bund's lights were dazzling. The bathtub by the window allowed me to soak while enjoying the magical Shanghai nightscape, creating an incredible atmosphere. The room was clean and tidy, the bedding soft and comfortable, soundproofing excellent, and all amenities were well-stocked.

The front desk service was thoughtful and efficient, making check-in a breeze. A special thanks to Manager Ba for the guidance.

The breakfast on the 56th floor offered a rich variety, and dining by the window provided a superb view. The location is perfect; you can walk to IFC and the Oriental Pearl Tower downstairs. This is my top choice for staying in Shanghai, highly recommended!

Of the three iconic buildings in Shanghai, Jin Mao Tower is my favorite. The hotel environment, facilities, and scenery are all fantastic and worth experiencing. The only downside is the huge number of people at breakfast, which shows how high the occupancy rate is. Overall, it's still great! 👍

I had a wonderful stay at the Grand Hyatt Jinmao! Judy's greetings were prompt, and check-out was quick and efficient. The hotel is elegantly and stylishly decorated, centrally located, and within walking distance of shopping districts, making it convenient for dining, entertainment, and leisure. Overall, a great experience!

Facilities: For such an old brand hotel, it can be seen that they are very attentive to the maintenance and management of facilities. Although there are traces of time, they are still able to keep up with the pace of the times.

Here's my take:
1. Some negative reviews mention poor service from the front desk or concierge. Perhaps it was an issue with a specific staff member or bad luck, but the front desk and concierge staff who assisted me provided good service.
2. The breakfast was quite varied, with separate Western and Chinese sections. The staff were very enthusiastic and guided me to a seat.
3. Overall, the room was clean. As an established five-star hotel, it certainly has a strong foundation. It would be even more perfect if it had smart toilets, but I understand that replacing all of them might lead to a lot of wasted toilet seats. 
Overall, I'm quite satisfied. I hope the hotel continues to maintain its excellent service and leaves all guests with positive experiences and memories.

We chose to stay at Grand Hyatt Shanghai, one of the three best hotels in Shanghai, for our wedding anniversary. We arrived at the hotel at around 1:00 pm. We were stopped before entering the parking lot. When we opened the trunk, a black dog came to sniff it. We took the parking lot elevator to the first floor and then changed to the hotel elevator to go directly to the 54th floor for check-in. We were greeted by Miss Shi at the front desk. She was pretty and very friendly. When we learned that we were here to celebrate our anniversary, Mr. Zhou and Mr. Zhu next to us were very happy to upgrade us to a river view suite with a view of the Oriental Pearl Tower. Because the room had not been cleaned yet, we were sent to the 83rd floor Guest House for afternoon tea☕️. We drank It's nice to have coffee while looking at the scenery of Lujiazui Bund while waiting for the room. When the room came out and we entered the room, we found that the hotel had prepared flowers for us 💐Thank you 😊. The room facilities are a bit old. After all, the hotel has been open for a long time. The TV on the double basin can't be turned on, and the bathroom sound system is broken. The water splashes outside easily when showering, and the shower head on the bathtub 🛁 can't be turned on. I hope the hotel can improve. The capsule coffee in the room is good, and the mineral water is also in sufficient supply. The mini bar needs to be paid, which is not good for the VIP room. In the evening 🌆 the happy hour on the 87th floor is suitable for taking photos and checking in. The scenery is very good. It is recommended to go there early for breakfast, otherwise you will have to wait for a table. The breakfast restaurant is very large and is divided into two sides, one side is Chinese food 🥢 and the other side is Western food 🍽️. The variety is very rich. Shanghai specialty snacks are available: salty soy milk, pan-fried steamed buns, pot stickers, rice cakes, scallion pancakes, fried dough sticks, etc. There are many varieties of Western food. I especially like smoked salmon, but there are fewer fruit varieties. The coffee ☕️ is very delicious! Parking for hotel guests 🚗 is free, which is better than the nearby hotels! We had a very pleasant anniversary, so happy 🥳 I will come again next time if I have the chance!
As always, I am very satisfied. I would like to thank Natty from the Guest Service Center for her patient and meticulous service. Highly recommended.

The breakfast offered a wide variety of choices, and the location was excellent, with convenient subway access. It's highly recommended for both business and leisure travelers. I will definitely choose Grand Hyatt Shanghai again on my next trip to Shanghai.

This was my second stay at the Grand Hyatt Jinmao, and it continues to maintain the consistent high standards of an established five-star hotel. The concierge staff proactively helped with my luggage and guided me attentively throughout the process. Check-in was very quick, so guests don't have to wait long. The room was exceptionally clean; there was no dust in the wardrobe or nightstand crevices, the bathroom was dry with no standing water, and the bedding was soft and comfortable against the skin. Sitting by the window, you get a panoramic view of Lujiazui – towering buildings by day and a dazzling cityscape by night. With convenient access to the subway and shopping malls nearby, it’s an excellent choice for accommodation in Shanghai, whether you're traveling for leisure or business.

The hotel is very well-maintained, the rooms are clean and dry, the service is thoughtful and non-intrusive, and the facilities are complete and functional. After much consideration, and out of respect and fondness for this Shanghai landmark, I'm giving it a 4.5-star rating. It's not quite a perfect score, but definitely 'top-tier' in its own right. Although the staff repeatedly asked me for a five-star review, even offering to write it for me and promising a free upgrade on my next stay, I still want to give my honest opinion:

1.  The outdated facilities are a fact. The power outlets weren't working, the bathroom curtain was rusted, and there was a strange smell in the room. However, you can tell that the quality of the items in this older landmark hotel is still very high. I liked the marble finishes, the hot water was quick to respond, the hairdryer was just like the one I have at home, the atrium was stunning and impressive, and the room key was unique.

2.  The service was standard. There were queues for check-in and also for meals. Perhaps because it was summer, there were a lot of tourists, and the lobby was as bustling as a marketplace every day. The most disappointing aspect was the restaurant – it was incredibly noisy, not just a little bit! While guests being loud is one thing, the staff constantly pushing utility carts around created a tremendous amount of noise; it was truly market-level chaos!

In comparison, I won't even mention the hardware; its age is understandable. But purely in terms of breakfast, it's nowhere near as good as the Conrad. This is my first long review, and I genuinely hope for improvements and optimization. Next time I stay, you don't need to upgrade me; just let me see a better Grand Hyatt.

The windows were spotless, and the city view, including the Oriental Pearl Tower and the Bund's World Expo complex at night, was breathtaking. The buffet had a wide variety of dishes and tasted great. As a landmark in Lujiazui, Pudong, it offers excellent value for money and was my top choice!

Compared to several high-rise hotels in Lujiazui, Grand Hyatt Jin Mao offers a balanced blend of value for money and comfort. The advantage of its high floor-to-ceiling windows is evident, preventing any feeling of being cooped up, and the soft furnishings are retro and tasteful. The soundproofing at night is excellent; you can't hear any traffic from below. Room service is prompt; extra bottled water was delivered within minutes of my call.

Grand Hyatt Shanghai remains one of Shanghai’s most iconic luxury hotels. The strongest selling points are its spectacular skyline views, location in the landmark Jin Mao Tower, spacious rooms, and excellent access to the Lujiazui financial district. However, several recent guests note that some room interiors and facilities are beginning to show their age compared with newer luxury competitors in Shanghai. Overall, it remains a highly recommended hotel for first-time visitors seeking a classic Shanghai skyline experience.

A wonderful stay, even though it was very short!

I only spent one night at this hotel, but I absolutely loved my experience!

The location is exceptional, and the view from our room was simply breathtaking! A stunning panorama of Shanghai, including the famous Oriental Pearl Tower and the surrounding skyscrapers. A true marvel, day and night!

The breakfast is excellent, plentiful, and varied. We also thoroughly enjoyed the Kobachi Japanese restaurant, both for the quality of its dishes and its warm welcome.

My son particularly appreciated the thoughtful touches from the hotel, especially the gift he received upon our departure: an adorable plush toy that he immediately adopted! A thoughtful gesture that delighted him immensely.

The staff is truly friendly, attentive, and professional, which makes the experience even more enjoyable.

I would like to express my sincere gratitude to Maggie Hu and Mia Xu, as well as to the person who kindly granted me a late check-out, whose name I unfortunately forget. I was particularly touched by their thoughtfulness and availability.

A truly wonderful experience, with service befitting this magnificent establishment. Despite the short duration of our stay, we will cherish the memories and will gladly return on our next trip to Shanghai!

I highly recommend the Grand Hyatt Shanghai!

My overall experience at Grand Hyatt Jin Mao was excellent this time. The front desk staff were very polite and efficient with check-in. They were also patient and helpful when I had questions. The room was meticulously cleaned, fresh, and odor-free, making for a comfortable stay. The hotel's facilities are well-maintained, and the public areas are grand and comfortable. The location is superb, convenient for both travel and shopping, making it suitable for both tourists and business travelers. I'll definitely choose this hotel again next time I'm in Shanghai.

This time, I stayed in a city view twin room. The hotel is located high up in the Jin Mao Tower, offering an excellent location with convenient access to Lujiazui. The Oriental Pearl TV Tower and IFC are within walking distance.
The room has a classic Chinese retro style. The twin beds are adequately sized, the bedding is comfortable, and the hygiene is well-maintained. The city view room overlooks the Lujiazui cityscape, and the city lights at night are dazzling, creating a wonderful atmosphere.

The guest rooms are well-maintained; despite being open for many years, the hardware is clean and looks brand new. The marble bathroom is spotless, and there are no signs of wear on the furniture. The air conditioning is remarkably quiet, and the temperature control is highly responsive, allowing for precise adjustments to the ideal temperature. Both down and memory foam pillows are provided, which can be swapped out as needed, ensuring a restful night's sleep that completely washes away any travel fatigue.

Although the Grand Hyatt Jin Mao, built in 1999, is showing its age—which lowered our expectations—it actually turned out to be a great stay. The doormen actively opened car doors and retrieved our luggage. The front desk accommodated our requests as much as possible, upgrading us to a Grand Club River View Room on the 80th floor facing the Puxi Bund. The room was well-maintained, feeling fresh and clean. In the Executive Lounge, the afternoon tea's blueberry scones and walnut cake were quite good (the coffee machine is located in the innermost corner), though the evening canapés were of mediocre quality—I had the salted salmon. Breakfast on the 56th floor was decent; if you walk to the northernmost buffet station and look inside, you'll find freshly pan-fried buns (shengjianbao) and potstickers, which were delicious. The room is 40 square meters, and the bathroom is small and compact. Still, it's totally worth visiting for the experience—both its exterior and interior are the most stunning among the 'three major skyscrapers'.

The stay exceeded my expectations! The hotel's location is excellent, situated in the prime area of ​​Lujiazui, making it convenient to go anywhere. The room was clean and tidy, spacious, and the panoramic floor-to-ceiling windows offered fantastic views, showcasing the river and city skyline. The service was also very attentive.

As a local from the capital, I drove through Shanghai to experience its charm. This time, I stayed at the Grand Hyatt Jin Mao, which offered an authentic and high-value way to experience the city.

The hotel is located in the Jin Mao Tower, one of Lujiazui's 'three-piece set,' so the location is excellent and includes free underground parking. Leaving the car at the hotel made it incredibly convenient to visit the Bund, Nanjing Road, Jing'an Temple, and the Oriental Pearl Tower, saving us the hassle of finding parking.

We booked a river view suite. Although the hotel dates back to 2014, it's exceptionally well-maintained, and the in-room amenities are up-to-date. From our high floor, the city views, both day and night, were absolutely stunning.

The lounge also offers great views, and the food and breakfast were decent, with good fruit. The evening views from the Cloud 9 restaurant were also fine. Spending a whole day at the hotel was a fantastic rest during our trip, and I would definitely choose to stay here again.
